analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. docs/reference/configuration.md adds two env-var rows at head lines 416-417: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md adds a paragraph (patch hunk around head lines 757-765) describing streamed `auto` tool-call fragments in inference_chunk deltas, plus a date bump. No source or control code is changed, so no control was weakened.

Relevant threats examined: T-008 (plaintext SSE on encryption failure) and TB-002. The new text says the chunk `data` field is empty when E2E encryption is active (unchanged context line). Tool-call fragments are carried in choices[].delta, which sits inside the same chunk payload. The docs do not say fragments leave that payload or bypass `encrypted_data`. The new streaming behavior's actual implementation (MLXOpenAIService.swift streamChatCompletionFrames, ToolStreamPreparation.swift) is not in the supplied evidence. An open question for deeper review is whether the fragmented tool-call chunks go through the same per-chunk encryption path and never emit plaintext `data` when encryption setup fails.

The doc says each streamed call is still validated when its frame closes. Streamed fragments reach the consumer before validation completes. That is a behavior/consumer-contract point, not a provider-custody regression, and the provider and consumer are an adversarial boundary only for provider outputs (T-007), which is unchanged.

Both env vars are documented as forwarded to the LaunchAgent. They are behavior toggles, not security overrides: the operator can only turn them off or leave them on, with no new trust or authorization effect. TB-011/T-053 (App Attest authorization) and T-041 (prefix cache) are unaffected.

No new attack surface or invalidated assumption is established from the supplied docs. Code-level verification of streaming encryption and tool-call validation belongs to the corresponding source PR.
